parameters.content: Normalizes Apollo's response shape across all search branches, dedupes by domain, and flattens each org into a clean row. Emits an error item (with raw_response / available_keys) if nothing came back.
Adds https://, strips trailing slash. Companies with no website but a LinkedIn URL are flagged and kept (routed through Has Website?); companies with neither are dropped.

For live sites: pulls title/meta/OG tags, H1/H2s, JSON-LD schema, nav-based signals (careers/pricing/blog), embedded tool fingerprints (Intercom, HubSpot, etc.), and runs healthcare + buying-signal keyword scans on CLEANED TEXT (not raw HTML).
Extracts the top-ranked person and stashes all found people as _raw_people.
Reshapes the top person into the fields Apollo's bulk_match endpoint expects.
If no decision maker was found, passes an empty person object through instead.
Merges enriched person data (with fallback to the original search result) onto the company record and builds the all_contacts list.
Strips markdown fences, extracts/parses the JSON, falls back to neutral defaults if parsing fails.

Computes a weighted 0-100 lead score from company size, tech signals, growth/automation scores, buying-signal count, contact completeness, funding, and healthcare fit; loops back to Loop Over Items1 for the next company.
After the loop: drops skipped/scoreless leads and sorts by score, reads existing sheet rows, dedupes by normalized website (and within the run), then keeps the top Max_lead NEW leads.
Builds a human-readable text report of the ranked leads and emails it.
LinkedIn-only companies skip the website fetch and go straight to signal check + decision-maker lookup.
Receives Apollo's async phone-reveal callback and writes the number into the Phone_lookup sheet (matched on Person ID). Verify the payload shape on the first real callback.

options.systemMessage:
=You are a senior B2B sales strategist and AI automation consultant.

Analyse the company information and website content provided.

Return ONLY a valid JSON object.
Do NOT return markdown.
Do NOT return explanations.
Do NOT wrap in code blocks.

Schema:
{
"industry": "",
"business_summary": "<2-3 sentence description of what the company does>",
"target_customer": "",
"automation_opportunities": "<3-5 highly relevant AI automation opportunities specific to this company>",
"key_pain_points": "<specific operational bottlenecks, inefficiencies, customer service issues, lead management issues, manual processes, scheduling, reporting, data entry, follow-up gaps, etc.>",
"personalized_message": "",
"ai_readiness": <integer 1-10>,
"automation_need": <integer 1-10>,
"growth_signal": <integer 1-10>
}

Message Writing Rules:
Generate a single personalized outreach paragraph.
Do NOT generate subject lines, greetings, sign-offs, or bullet points.
The message should start directly with an observation about the company, mention the company name naturally, reference at least one identified pain point and one automation opportunity.
Focus on business outcomes: saving time, reducing costs, increasing revenue, improving response times, eliminating manual work.
Be between 60 and 120 words. Sound professional and consultative.
End naturally with: "Would you be open to a quick 15-minute conversation next week?"
Return the entire message as ONE continuous paragraph in the field: "personalized_message"

Scoring Guide:
ai_readiness: 1-3=little tech adoption, 4-7=modern tools, 8-10=highly tech-driven
automation_need: 1-3=limited opportunities, 4-7=moderate potential, 8-10=strong manual workflows
growth_signal: 1-3=little evidence, 4-7=moderate indicators, 8-10=strong indicators

If website content is empty or fewer than 200 characters: set ai_readiness=3, automation_need=5, growth_signal=3 (neutral defaults, not punished to 1), and note insufficient website data in business_summary but still use Apollo description.

Return raw JSON only.
